# Vibe code

The user describes a change in a sentence or two — "let managers approve orders",
"show the customer's open orders on their page" — and expects it built. This
workflow keeps that loop short **and** holds every change to the same gates, so
speed never costs security, a broken build, untested logic or an undocumented
change.

The gates are not a checklist you tick. `./mxcli workflow check` runs them and
records what they answered in the run's file under `docs/brain/workflows/`, and
`./mxcli workflow close` refuses while a blocking one fails.

| Gate | Blocks | Decided by |
|---|---|---|
| Intent | yes | the run has a one-sentence intent |
| Security | yes | `mxcli lint` reports no security finding (SEC*, MPR007) that was not there when the run started |
| Builds | yes | `mxcli docker check` (mx check) reports no error |
| Tests | yes | `tests/` exists and `mxcli test tests/ --local` passes |
| Quality | no | `mxcli report` score is not below the run's start |
| Change note | yes | the run has a change note |

## The loop

Use `./mxcli` as the project's other skills do, with `-p <App>.mpr`.

### 1. Intent — one sentence, then start the run

Restate what the user asked as one sentence a reviewer would understand, and
confirm it with them only if it is genuinely ambiguous. Then:

```bash
./mxcli workflow start vibe "<the intent, one sentence>" -p <App>.mpr
```

If `./mxcli workflow status` shows an open vibe run for the same intent, continue
that one instead of starting another.

### 2. Change the model — smallest change that does it

- Read the matching skill before writing MDL (`mdl-entities`, `create-page`,
  `write-microflows`, … — their descriptions say when).
- Write the change as a script in `mdlsource/<topic>.mdl` starting with `mdl 1;`,
  using `create or modify` so it can be re-run. `check`, then `exec`, then `exec`
  again: the second run must write nothing.
- Keep it small. A second, unrelated change is a second run.

### 3. Security — in the same script, not afterwards

Every new entity needs access rules, every new microflow and page needs allowed
roles, and a new home page must be reachable by the roles that land on it. Read
`manage-security` if unsure which role gets what. A change that only works for
an Administrator is not done.

### 4. Look — use the theme, not inline styles

New pages use Atlas classes and the project's theme (`atlas-design`,
`theme-styling`); no hard-coded colours or inline styles. No gate measures this
yet — say in the change note what you did.

### 5. Tests — for the logic you added or changed

Add or extend a test in `tests/<topic>.test.mdl` for each microflow whose
behaviour you added or changed (`test-microflows`). A pure page or styling change
needs no new test, but the existing ones must still pass.

### 6. Check the gates

```bash
./mxcli workflow check -p <App>.mpr
```

Fix every ✗ and run it again. A `!` (Quality) does not block: look at what
lowered the score, fix it if it is yours, and say in the note if you leave it.
Never edit the run's file to change a result.

### 7. Change note — a few lines a reviewer can read

```bash
./mxcli workflow note "<what changed and why: elements added or changed, roles granted, tests added, anything left>" -p <App>.mpr
./mxcli workflow check -p <App>.mpr
./mxcli workflow close -p <App>.mpr
```

The note is the change's documentation. It stays in `docs/brain/workflows/` with
the gate results, so a reviewer sees what changed and that it was checked.

### 8. Report and loop

Tell the user, in a few lines: what changed, which gates passed, anything left
(a `!`, a styling choice). Then ask what to change next — the next change is a
new run.

## When a gate cannot pass

- **No `tests/` yet**: create `tests/` with a first test for the logic you just
  added. The workflow does not accept "no tests" for a change with logic.
- **The build fails on something you did not touch**: say so, show the error,
  and ask the user whether to fix it in this run or start one for it. Do not
  close the run.
- **Security findings that predate the change** do not block: the gate holds the
  change to adding none, and `check` says how many were there before. Fix one if
  it is small and in the module you touched; otherwise mention it to the user
  and record it with `./mxcli brain capture`.
